```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A's demand evidence includes specific, sourced price points that buyers already pay or have paid ($8→$34/mo, $15/mo, $20/mo, $79/mo). This shows an existing habit of paying for the category. B's demand quotes describe pain but contain no price or willingness-to-pay signal.",
    "A has a sourced $0-cash acquisition channel with a documented first-customer outcome: a Product Hunt launch with 559 upvotes and Product of the Day for Instatus. That suits a 90-day first-customer goal. B's only priced channel is paid search at $10-13 CPC, and its organic channel is described as already contested by every direct competitor.",
    "A's sourced paid-search benchmark ($4.66 average CPC) is roughly a third of B's sourced $10-13 CPC. That lowers the cost of testing for a first paying customer.",
    "A's core product is shown, per its sources, to be buildable in days by solo builders on simple stacks. B's own Case Against says the differentiating capability, continuous multi-jurisdiction rule-change monitoring, is an ongoing data burden. B also says a six-week build would likely ship only a subset of what $29-49/mo competitors already offer.",
    "Both briefs admit heavy saturation and no clear wedge, so competition does not separate them. On that tie, A's stronger payment and channel evidence decides it."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence is three Reddit posts from a solo structural engineer, an HR practitioner, and a therapist. None states a price paid or a willingness to pay, and none comes from the stated buyer (finance/ops leads at small multi-state firms). The HR post criticizes 'big systems' rather than validating a standalone tracker. B's '~$14.50 RegTech CPC' figure has no source and counts as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe saturated markets with no identified wedge, and neither gives conversion, churn, or CAC data for a new entrant. A has its own sourcing gaps. Hyperping's '~$15K MRR' is unsourced. Instatus's '$40K MRR' is cited only to a pricing page, so it is effectively unsourced. A's demand quotes come from people who built their own alternatives, which signals price sensitivity and DIY substitution as much as demand. A wins mainly on sourced evidence of existing payment behavior and a cheap, documented launch channel. That edge is modest."
}
```
